newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Antex Biologics starts trials.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Antex Biologics starts trials.

text.p: Antex Biologics Inc began clinical trials of its second and third vaccines this week, the company's chief executive, Vic Esposito, told Reuters on Wednesday.
The company's first vaccine, which began Phase I trials in 1995, is expected to begin Phase II trials this year.

Antex had its first profitable year in 1996, earning about $560,000 on revenues of $3.8 million from milestone payments, research and development funding and small business innovation research grants, Esposito said.
The company has yet to release its fourth-quarter and full year results.

It previously reported nine-month earnings of $611,240, or $0.03 per share, on revenues of nearly $3.1 million. That indicates a fourth-quarter loss of about $60,000 on revenues of $700,000. That compares to a third-quarter loss of $157,551 on revenues of $623,646.
The quarterly fluctuations will persist for the forseeable future, Esposito said, as the cost of clinical trials was spread unevenly throughout the year.
He said he expected Antex to turn a profit on an annual basis.

The U.S. Navy is funding clinical trials of Campylobacter, Antex's initial vaccine, designed to control diarrhea. That disease disabled more U.S. military personnel than the Iraqi armed forces did during the Persian Gulf War, Esposito said.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc is funding development of Antex's Haemophilus influenzae otitis media vaccine with milestone payments. Otitis media, a common ear infection, is the leading infectious disease for infants and children. It is increasingly resistant to antibiotics.
Phase I testing of that vaccine began this week, he said.
Under a joint venture agreement with SmithKline Beecham Plc, Antex also began Phase I tests of its Helicobacter vaccine for gastritis, peptic ulcers and stomach cancer.
